newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-RIO DE JANEIRO CHAMPIONSHIP HIT BY WALKOUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RIO DE JANEIRO CHAMPIONSHIP HIT BY WALKOUT.

text.p: The Rio de Janeiro championship got off to a chaotic start on Sunday when half of the games were cancelled after three of the four major clubs involved decided to boycott the tournament.

Botafogo, Fluminense and defending champions Flamengo all refused to play in protest at the format of the 12-team tournament, which they claimed forced them to play too many games against minor opposition.
As a result, only three of the six matches scheduled for the weekend took place.
Vasco da Gama, the only major club to stay in the competition, beat Bangu 3-0 before a meagre 1,600 attendance.
Vasco themselves were without star striker Edmundo, who refused to take part in pre-season training because of a row over his contract and was then suspended by the club.
Instead, Edmundo, a hugely talented but explosive player, took part in a beach soccer match on Rio's famous Copacabana beach.

There were rumours that the rebel clubs would attempt to patch up their differences with the Rio de Janeiro football federation, which organises the competition, but it was not clear exactly what would happen next.
The rebel clubs decided to abandon the competition at a meeting on Friday.
"Anyone with any sense can see that there is no way we can take part in the competition that Vasco and the Rio federation want," said Fluminense president Alvaro Barcelos.
Brazil is unique among major soccer nations in devoting half of its season to regional competitions. Critics have called for the system to be scrapped and replaced by a single national competition.
The Rio tournament is the second-most important regional competition, behind the Sao Paulo championship which is due to start in early February.
Before that, a Rio-Sao Paulo tournament is due to take place, starting on Saturday.
